titles: Crossed $30K? When Freelancers Must Charge GST (Canada)
The $30,000 GST Rule Isn't Per Year
Freelancers: When Do You Have to Register for GST/HST?
yt.description:
Freelancing in Canada and getting close to $30,000? The GST/HST threshold isn't counted per calendar year. It's any four consecutive calendar quarters.

Example: $5,000 + $8,000 + $9,000 + $9,500 over four quarters = $31,500, over the line. You stop being a small supplier at the end of the month after that quarter, then you have 29 days to register. Cross $30,000 in a single quarter and you charge GST/HST on the very sale that put you over.

After that, a $1,000 invoice in Manitoba carries $50 of GST. That $50 was never yours. The upside: GST/HST you pay on business costs comes back as input tax credits. HST provinces charge 13–15%, and provincial sales taxes have their own rules.

Source: CRA, "When to register for and start charging the GST/HST" (canada.ca). Example only; general information, not tax advice.

_vo: You just crossed thirty thousand dollars in sales. Did you just become a tax collector? For G-S-T, thirty thousand isn't per year. It's any four calendar quarters in a row. Say you billed five thousand, then eight, then nine, then nine and a half. That's thirty-one thousand, five hundred. Over the line. You stop being a small supplier at the end of the next month. Then you have twenty-nine days to register. Cross thirty thousand in a single quarter? You charge G-S-T on the very sale that put you over. After that, a thousand-dollar invoice in Manitoba carries fifty dollars of G-S-T. That fifty was never yours. You collect it for the government. The upside: G-S-T you pay on business costs comes back as input tax credits. In H-S-T provinces it's thirteen to fifteen percent. And provincial sales taxes have their own rules. Watch your last four quarters, not your tax year.
